Return results

Source: vignettes/returning-results.Rmd
returning-results.Rmd
library(mcplite)

Start with ordinary R return values. Use tool_result() when a client needs structured data, rich content, result metadata, or an explicit tool-level error. This guide builds on Write tools; the examples run without starting a server.

Return an ordinary value

A tool can return a calculation, a string, or a named list directly:

inventory_value <- list(item = "coffee", count = 0L)
inventory_value
#> $item
#> [1] "coffee"
#> 
#> $count
#> [1] 0

For a tool return, character values become literal text; character vectors are joined with newlines. Other JSON-serializable values, such as this list, become JSON in a text content block. Bare lists are ordinary values, not MCP result objects. Returning a JSON-looking string does not opt into structured content.

See Return-value mappings for exact empty, missing, scalar, and array mappings. The distinction matters if a client or output schema expects a particular JSON shape.

Add structured data

Return tool_result(structured_content = value) when a client should receive machine-readable data as well as text:

result <- tool_result(
  structured_content = list(item = "coffee", count = 0L),
  meta = list(source = "local inventory")
)
result$content[[1]]$text
#> [1] "{\"item\":\"coffee\",\"count\":0}"

When you omit content, tool_result() generates one JSON text fallback block. If you supply content explicitly, it is kept without an extra fallback:

tool_result(
  content = content_text("Coffee is out of stock."),
  structured_content = list(item = "coffee", count = 0L)
)

Choose text that remains useful on its own: older protocols can omit structured content or restrict its shape. The compatibility table shows what each supported version receives. JSON-looking strings, including jsonlite json objects, remain string values in structured content; they are not parsed or inserted as raw JSON.

Include rich content

Build an ordered list of content_*() blocks. For example, return a short summary with a self-contained text resource:

tool_result(content = list(
  content_text("Inventory snapshot attached."),
  content_resource(
    uri = "inventory:snapshot",
    text = "item,count\ncoffee,0\ntea,5\n",
    mime_type = "text/csv"
  )
))

The content constructors also support images, audio, and resource links, with optional annotations and metadata. Image, audio, and resource blob payloads must already be base64-encoded: the constructors do not read files, download URLs, infer MIME types, or encode the data. Tool authors own payload integrity, access checks, and size limits.

A resource link carries your URI; it does not add a resource endpoint or make the URI readable through the server. Audio, resource links, and per-content metadata require MCP 2025-06-18 or later. A 2024-11-05 call returning audio or a resource link receives a contained tool-level error, not partial content.

For expected failures, set is_error = TRUE as shown in Report failures.

Advertise structured output

Use output_schema on the tool to describe its structured result. This example returns an array of strings:

search_items <- tool(
  function(query) {
    matches <- paste(query, c("alpha", "beta"), sep = "-")
    tool_result(structured_content = matches)
  },
  name = "search_items",
  description = "Find local items whose names start with a query.",
  arguments = list(query = type_string()),
  output_schema = type_array(type_string())
)
search_items("tea")$structured_content
#> [1] "tea-alpha" "tea-beta"

The schema is descriptive: mcplite checks container shape and serializability, not full schema validity or result conformance. The tool owns those guarantees. Modern MCP 2026-07-28 clients can receive this array schema and structured value; legacy clients cannot. The tool remains available and the generated text fallback still represents the matches. See the compatibility table for object-shaped results and other versions.

Choose payload encoding at startup

If default JSON mappings do not fit your payload, set package-global options near the top of the server script, before constructing results and calling mcp_server(). Keep them stable while the server runs. The results reference lists the defaults, supported choices, and an executable example.

These options affect payload values, not protocol fields, schemas, annotations, or result and content metadata. The tool still owns output-schema conformance. For a per-tool text representation, return your own JSON as ordinary character text, for example as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(value, na = "null")); it stays literal text rather than becoming structured content.
